title: Foundations: Frappe Team par Agent Anatomy, Primitives aur Agent Contract
summary: Seekho ki agent ko prompt ya template se kya alag karta hai, ek agent ko baarah anatomy elements mein tod kar har ek ko us Claude Code mechanism se map karo jo use implement karta hai (ya maano ki woh sirf convention hai), in elements ko aaj Frappe team par DocType JSON, patches aur fixtures review karne walon par map karo, prompt, skill, agent, workflow, MCP server, Claude Code hook aur Frappe hook mein sahi choice karo, aur spice_lite reviewer ke liye apna pehla Agent Contract likho, jise tum khud ek validator chala kar check karoge.
prerequisites: Claude Code CLI installed aur authenticated (`claude --version`)
Ek bench jisme `spice_lite` `test.localhost` par installed ho (`sample-app/scripts/setup-bench.sh`)
Frappe whitelisted method aur DocType JSON file padhne mein comfort

concepts.heading: Prompt, template, agent: asal mein kya alag hai
Agent anatomy: baarah elements
concepts.body_md:
Is course ka har agent inhi baarah elements se specify hota hai. "Chat mein ek baar chal gaya tha" wale prompts ki zyada failures inme se kisi ek ko implicit chhodne se aati hain.

1. **Responsibilities**: ek kaam. Do kaam (review *aur* fix, ya review *aur* migrate) matlab do agents.
2. **Boundaries**: kya scope se bahar hai, chahe agent use kar sakta ho.
3. **Inputs**: task message mein exactly kya aata hai (base ref, run id, handoff path). Subagent ke paas tumse aur kuch nahi hota.
4. **Outputs**: artifact aur uska format, itna precise ki script check kar sake.
5. **Tools**: allowlist, waise spelled jaise Claude Code tools ko spell karta hai (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Bash`, `mcp__server__tool`), Bash scope likh kar (sirf `git diff`; sirf `bench --site test.localhost run-tests`).
6. **Context**: kaunsa project knowledge woh automatically load karta hai (CLAUDE.md, path-scoped `.claude/rules/`, preloaded skills) aur is task ke liye use kaunsi files `Read` karni hain (`context/standards/frappe-coding-standards.md`).
7. **Instructions**: procedure, persona nahi. "Tum ek senior Frappe developer ho" koi step nahi hai.
8. **Memory/state**: runs ke beech kya bachta hai (`memory` field, ya handoff files) aur kya jaan-boojh kar nahi bachta.
9. **Permissions**: bina pooche kya kar sakta hai, kiske liye human chahiye (`bench --site * migrate`), kya denied hai (`Read(**/site_config.json)`, `bench drop-site`).
10. **Verification**: koi bhi kaise bata sake ki output achha hai ya sirf plausible.
11. **Failure handling**: jab input kharab ho ya kaam bahut bada ho tab woh guess karne ki jagah kya karta hai.
12. **Handoffs**: structured artifact jo agla step consume karta hai.

Neeche ki table *Anatomy element to Claude Code mechanism* har element ko us real configuration se map karti hai jo use implement karti hai. Pattern dekho: elements 1, 5, 6, 7, 8 aur 9 ke first-class Claude Code fields hain; elements 2, 3, 4, 10, 11 aur 12 zyadatar **conventions** hain jab tak tum koi Claude Code hook, permission rule ya eval nahi jodte jo unhe enforce kare. Modules 05, 08, 09 aur 10 zyadatar inhi conventions ko mechanisms mein badalne ke liye hain.

Exercise `01-anatomy-breakdown` yeh list `spice_lite/api/fhir.py` ke against ek real one-off review prompt par apply karti hai aur dikhati hai ki woh kaunse elements undefined chhodta hai.

concepts.heading: Frappe team par anatomy: DocType JSON, patches aur fixtures kaun review karta hai
concepts.body_md:
Agents design karne se pehle likho ki aaj kaam kaun karta hai. `spice_next_core` jaisi Frappe team par change shayad hi kabhi sirf Python hota hai, aur review kai logon mein bata hota hai:

- **Core maintainer** DocType JSON diff padhta hai: bina `search_index` ka naya field, aisa `autoname` jo documents ka naam MRN se rakhe, wide kiya gaya `permissions` array. Review-standards bina patch ke schema change, ya bina security review ke permissions change ko kam se kam `high` banata hai.
- **Jo releases own karta hai** woh `patches.txt` padhta hai: naya patch `[pre_model_sync]` mein hai ya `[post_model_sync]` mein, kya woh idempotent hai, aur kya kisi ne existing line edit ki? Patch Log exact line text record karta hai, isliye edit kiya gaya comment patch ko har country site par dobara chala deta hai (FRAPPE_FACTS §11).
- **Country lead** fixtures padhta hai: Custom Field aur Property Setter fixtures country app mein belong karte hain, `spice_lite` mein nahi (frappe-coding-standards rule 12). Fixtures har migrate par overwrite hote hain, isliye bhatka hua fixture chupchaap jeet jaata hai.
- **Site access wala koi** merge ke baad shared site par `bench --site <site> migrate` chalata hai.

Inme se har insaan ek implicit agent hai jiski implicit anatomy hai: ek **responsibility** (JSON, patch order), ek **context** (unhe pata hai ki `frappe.get_all` permissions skip karta hai), ek **permission** (inme se sirf ek migrate kar sakta hai), aur ek **human gate** (PR approval). Inhe agents banane ka matlab hai yeh sab likhna:

- `reviewer` ko DocType JSON, `patches.txt`, `hooks.py` aur fixture checks **must** rules ke roop mein milte hain, aur jab Claude un files ke saath kaam karta hai tab `.claude/rules/doctype-json.md` woh context deta hai (ek path-scoped rule; docs yeh nahi batate ki subagent ke reads ise trigger karte hain ya nahi, isliye agent body bhi Read karne wali file ka naam leti hai);
- jab bhi `permissions` array, `@frappe.whitelist` decorator ya `ignore_permissions` badalta hai tab `security` agent `next` step hai, jo reviewer ki ek **failure condition** hai;
- `migrate` insaan ke paas rehta hai: `.claude/settings.json` mein ek `ask` rule aur CLAUDE.md rule 9 ise **human gate** banate hain, kisi agent ka tool nahi.

Neeche ki comparison table *Frappe review surface to agent anatomy* har surface list karti hai. Isliye practically, Agent Contract ka pehla draft un logon ke saath interview hai jo aaj tumhara DocType JSON review karte hain.

concepts.heading: Mechanism ya convention: enforced vs requested
concepts.body_md:
Module 00 ne rule bataya tha: **instructions intent batati hain, permissions aur Claude Code hooks use enforce karte hain.** Yeh module ise aadat banata hai: agent ke liye likha har rule inme se ek label paata hai.

**Mechanism** woh cheez hai jo Claude Code khud karta hai, model chahe jo decide kare:

- `tools: Read, Grep, Glob` ka matlab hai ki `Edit` agent ke toolset mein nahi hai. Use `sl_patient.json` edit karne ke liye manaya nahi ja sakta.
- `.claude/settings.json` mein `permissions.deny: ["Read(**/site_config.json)"]` har agent ke liye read block karta hai.
- `permissionMode: dontAsk` har us cheez ko auto-deny karta hai jo prompt karti. Is repo mein `bench --site * console`, `execute` aur `migrate` `ask` rules hain, isliye `dontAsk` reviewer ko woh refuse ho jaate hain, human se poocha nahi jaata.
- `.claude/hooks/block-secrets.mjs` `Edit|Write` par ek Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook hai; yeh **2** se exit karta hai, jo call block karta hai. Exit 1 block nahi karta. Settings hooks subagents ke andar bhi fire hote hain.

**Convention** woh cheez hai jo sirf koi insaan, script ya eval check karta hai: six-field finding format, "standard cite karo", "kabhi LGTM mat likho", "`patches.txt` ko JSON ke saath review karo", handoff front matter jab tak module 08 `check-handoff.mjs` nahi jodta.

Conventions buri nahi hain; contract ka zyada hissa convention hi hai. Failure mode yeh maanna hai ki convention mechanism hai. Teen real traps:

- `dontAsk` sirf wahi deny karta hai jo prompt karta. `Bash(bench --site test.localhost run-tests *)` project **allow** list par hai, isliye `dontAsk` reviewer ab bhi test suite chala sakta hai. Ise git tak restrict karne ke liye agent-scoped Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook chahiye (module 05).
- Jab parent session `bypassPermissions`, `acceptEdits` ya `auto` mein chalta hai tab subagent ka `permissionMode` **ignore** hota hai. Wahi Claude Code hook durable guard hai.
- Skill `allowed-tools` turn ke liye tools ko **pre-approve** karta hai; unhe restrict nahi karta. Kisi ko hataane ke liye `disallowed-tools` use karo.

Isliye practically, Agent Contract ki har `must` aur `mustNot` line `[mechanism: ...]` ya `[convention: ...]` se khatam hoti hai, aur `validate-contract.mjs` us line ko reject karta hai jisme dono mein se kuch nahi. Jab kisi `mustNot` mein sirf conventions hon, validator warn karta hai: us agent ki boundaries poori tarah model ke theek behave karne par depend karti hain.

concepts.heading: Chhe Claude Code primitives, ek Frappe hook, aur choose kaise karein
concepts.body_md:
Claude Code SDLC automation ke liye chhe building blocks deta hai: **prompt, skill, agent, workflow, MCP server, Claude Code hook**. Frappe team ke paas ek saatvi cheez hai jise hook kehte hain aur jo Claude Code primitive bilkul nahi hai: **Frappe hook**, app ke `hooks.py` mein ek entry (`doc_events`, `scheduler_events`, `permission_query_conditions`, `fixtures`, `after_migrate`, ...). Yeh product code hai jo site ke andar chalta hai, jab koi clinician form save kare ya scheduler tick kare. Claude Code hook developer ki machine par chalta hai, jab Claude koi tool call karta hai.

Yeh takraav academic nahi hai. "Ek hook add karo jo secrets block kare" wala ticket `hooks.py` mein `doc_events` entry ban sakta hai; "jab Observation finalise ho tab hook chalao" `settings.json` mein `PostToolUse` entry ban sakta hai jo tab fire hoti hai jab Claude file likhta hai. Isiliye CLAUDE.md rule 5 akele shabd ko ban karta hai, validator us par warn karta hai, aur exercise `01-classify-primitives` ka grader akele `hook` ko `AMBIGUOUS` score karta hai.

Yeh decision order use karo; pehla "haan" jeet-ta hai (answer key ka logic bhi yahi hai):

0. **Kya yeh site par chalte app ka behaviour hai?** Toh yeh **Frappe hook** ya controller method hai, aur yeh kisi bhi code change ki tarah normal workflow se ship hota hai.
1. **Kya yeh har baar hona chahiye jab Claude kuch kare**, model ko yaad rahe ya na rahe? **Claude Code hook** (ya permission rule) use karo: secrets scanning, handoff validation, `patches.txt` ki applied line ke edits block karna.
2. **Kya ise repo ke bahar ka data ya actions chahiye** (Jira, GitHub, kisi site ka Frappe REST API)? **MCP server** use karo, taaki access ek named tool ho (`mcp__<server>__<tool>`) jise permission rules allow ya deny kar sakein.
3. **Kya yeh kai roles ko unke beech human gates ke saath chain karta hai?** `workflows/` mein ek **workflow** use karo, main session se chalaya hua (module 08).
4. **Kya ise apna context, apni tool limits, ya independent opinion chahiye?** **Agent** use karo.
5. **Kya wahi procedure log ya agents baar-baar karenge?** **Skill** use karo. Agents `skills` field se skills preload karte hain.
6. Warna yeh **prompt** hai.

Do combinations baar-baar aate hain: **agent + preloaded skill** (`reviewer` `code-review` preload karta hai; `sre` `production-rca` preload karta hai) aur **workflow + Claude Code hooks** (workflow order aur gates define karta hai; Claude Code hooks gates ko real banate hain).

concepts.heading: Agent Contract
concepts.body_md:
**Agent Contract** is course ka agent specification hai, jo agent file se pehle likha jaata hai aur uske bagal mein rakha jaata hai. Yeh convention hai, Claude Code feature nahi: Claude Code sirf `.claude/agents/<name>.md` padhta hai. Contract woh hai jiske against woh file review hoti hai, jise module 09 ke evals score karte hain, aur jise naya team member sabse pehle padhta hai.

Gyarah fields, `build/schema.json` ke `agentContracts` jaise hi:

| Field | Kis sawaal ka jawab deta hai |
|---|---|
| `purpose` | Output kaunse ek decision ko support karta hai? |
| `inputs` / `outputs` | Task message mein kya aata hai; kya wapas aata hai aur kahan save hota hai |
| `tools` | Exact tool names, scope ke saath ("Bash (only `git diff`, `git log`, `git status`)") |
| `permissions` | Kaunsa frontmatter aur settings boundary enforce karte hain |
| `must` / `mustNot` | Required aur forbidden behaviour, har ek mechanism ya convention se tagged |
| `failureConditions` | Kab guess karne ki jagah `blocked` ya `needs-human` ke saath rukna hai |
| `validation` | Woh command, eval ya check jo output ko acceptable prove kare |
| `handoffFormat` | Run-folder file aur uska front matter |
| `humanGate` | Insaan kahan approve karta hai, aur woh real mechanism jo unka intezaar karta hai |

Reusable template `AI-SDLC-frappe/agents/CONTRACT_TEMPLATE.md` hai; har roster agent ki bhari hui copy `AI-SDLC-frappe/agents/<agent>/CONTRACT.md` par rehti hai. `AI-SDLC-frappe/docs/foundations/validate-contract.mjs` check karta hai ki saare gyarah `## field` headings maujood aur order mein hain, list fields bullets hain, tool names real Claude Code tools hain, har `must`/`mustNot` line apna enforcement batati hai, `humanGate` ek real mechanism ka naam leta hai, aur do Frappe rules: Bash scope `bench console`, `execute`, `drop-site` ya `reinstall` grant nahi kar sakta, aur `migrate` scope ko bolna chahiye ki woh `ask` rule ke peeche hai. Akela "hook" ek warning hai. `--json` contract ko schema-shaped object ke roop mein print karta hai.

Yeh module ek worked **reviewer** draft (`docs/foundations/reviewer-contract-draft.md`) aur paanch planted mistakes wala ek first attempt ship karta hai. Module 02 jaan-boojh kar simple pehla reviewer banata hai, module 05-agent-roster is contract ko runtime definition ke saath `agents/reviewer/CONTRACT.md` ke roop mein finalise karta hai, aur module 09 agent ko iske against measure karta hai. Isliye practically, contract code ki tarah review se badalta hai, aur agent file uske peeche chalti hai.

concepts.heading: Handoffs aur depth: roster flat kyon rehta hai
concepts.body_md:
Is course ke agents kabhi seedhe ek doosre se baat nahi karte. Har ek ek **handoff** return karta hai: YAML front matter (`run_id`, `step`, `agent`, `status`, `inputs`, `next`) wala Markdown document jo `.ai-sdlc/runs/<run-id>/NN-<agent>.md` mein save hota hai. Agla agent file padhta hai, pichhle agent ki conversation nahi, kyonki uske paas woh hai hi nahi.

Claude Code gehre structures allow karta hai: current docs ke hisaab se subagent apne subagents spawn **kar sakta hai**, aur `Agent(...)` type allowlist sirf main thread ke roop mein chal rahe agent ke liye enforce hoti hai. Exact limits aur settings module 07-agent-composition mein sikhaye jaate hain.

In facts par bana is course ka design decision:

- **orchestrator** main thread ke roop mein chalta hai (`claude --agent orchestrator`, ya main session mein `/feature` skill). Delegation sirf yahin hota hai.
- Roster agents (`architect`, `developer`, `reviewer`, `tester`, `security`, `sre`) `tools` mein `Agent` list **nahi** karte. Woh depth 1 par chalte hain, isliye har delegation ek jagah dikhta hai aur har handoff ek file hai jise tum audit kar sakte ho.

Frappe change par flat chain ka concrete fayda hai. Jo feature `sl_observation.json`, controller, ek patch aur tests ko chhoota hai, woh `workflows/feature-delivery.md` ke order mein ek developer handoff, `bench --site test.localhost run-tests` result ke saath ek tester handoff aur ek security handoff (mandatory kyonki `permissions` array badla), phir ek reviewer handoff produce karta hai. Insaan chaar files padhta hai aur decide karta hai; kisi ko reconstruct nahi karna padta ki kis nested agent ne `migrate` chalaya, kyonki koi agent chala hi nahi sakta.

Anatomy ke liye iska matlab hai ki element 12 (handoffs) aur element 2 (boundaries) milte hain: `tools` se `Agent` ko bahar rakhna ek mechanism hai jo handoff chain ko linear rakhta hai. Reviewer draft ka `mustNot` ise bilkul isi roop mein record karta hai.

01-anatomy-breakdown.title: Ek one-off Frappe review prompt ko agent anatomy mein todo
01-anatomy-breakdown.objective: Woh review prompt lo jo aaj ek Frappe developer chat mein paste karta hai (woh model se `bench console` kholne aur `migrate` chalane ko bhi kehta hai), ise real `spice_lite/api/fhir.py` aur `sl_patient.json` ke against plan mode mein ek baar chalao, phir ise baarah anatomy elements mein todo. Har element ke liye record karo ki prompt kya kehta hai, gap kya hai, aur kaunsa Claude Code mechanism (ya convention) use `reviewer` agent mein implement karega. Aakhir mein woh Frappe review surfaces likho jo prompt bhool gaya.

evaluationCriteria: Baarah mein se har element ka ek concrete gap hai, jahan prompt kuch kehta hai wahan se quote kiya hua.
Claude Code column sirf build/CLAUDE_CODE_FACTS.md ke fields aur settings use karta hai (koi `temperature` nahi, agent mein hyphenated `allowed-tools` nahi).
Conventions ko conventions label kiya gaya hai, mechanisms bana kar nahi dikhaya.
Breakdown pehchanta hai ki "Fix anything obvious" aur "run migrate" do responsibilities jodte hain aur write aur site authority grant karte hain.
`bench console` ko ek arbitrary-code tool ke roop mein pehchana gaya hai jo kisi reviewer ke paas nahi hota, us `ask` rule ke saath jo pehle se use guard karta hai.
Frappe surfaces table DocType JSON, `patches.txt`, `hooks.py` aur fixtures ka naam leti hai, aur batati hai ki har rule kahan se aata hai.
improvements: Ek one-off security prompt ("check fhir.py for permission problems") ke liye breakdown dohraao aur compare karo ki `security` vs `reviewer` ke liye kaunse elements mechanisms hain.
Ek column jodo: kaunsa baad ka module har convention ko mechanism mein badalta hai.
Raw prompt teen baar chalao aur record karo ki runs ke beech kitne findings alag hain; yahi variance fixed output format ka argument hai.

01-classify-primitives.title: Baarah needs ko Claude Code primitive ya Frappe hook mein classify karo
01-classify-primitives.objective: Frappe team ke SDLC ki baarah real needs ke liye woh ek answer chuno jo fit ho (`prompt`, `skill`, `agent`, `workflow`, `mcp`, `claude-code-hook`, ya `frappe-hook`) aur ek sentence mein justify karo. Answer key ke against script se khud ko grade karo, phir jo miss hua uska justification padho. Do needs "hook" shabd par bane traps hain; akela `hook` zero score karta hai.

testCases.name: Grader example attempt ko pass karta hai
Zyada strict pass mark use fail karta hai
Khaali starting file zero score karti hai
Key examples real files ki taraf point karte hain
testCases.expected: 1 aur 1: N01 example woh Claude Code hook hai jo aaj exist karta hai, aur N11 Frappe hook example `hooks.py` mein commented `doc_events` block hai.

testCases.name: Grader aur key ke unit tests

evaluationCriteria: Grader ke saath kam se kam 10/12 score.
Har justification us property ka naam leta hai jisne decide kiya (runtime app behaviour, enforcement, external system, gates, isolation, reuse), sirf primitive ka naam nahi.
N01, N08 aur N12 ko Claude jo karta hai uske enforcement (Claude Code hooks) ke roop mein pehchana gaya, instruction problems ke roop mein nahi.
N11 ko Frappe hook (country app mein `doc_events`) aur N12 ko Claude Code hook ke roop mein pehchana gaya, is reason ke saath ki har trap trap kyon hai.
N09 ke liye `skill` answer saaf bolta hai ki skill `sre` agent ki tool boundary ke andar chalti hai.
improvements: Apni team ke backlog se paanch needs key mein jodo (jaise nightly `scheduler_events` job, ya check ki har DocType JSON change ke saath patch hai), har ek ke justification ke saath, aur kisi colleague se khud ko grade karwao.
Grader ko extend karo taaki woh us answer ko fail kare jiske `why` mein decision-order ka koi keyword na ho.
N12 guard banao: `Edit` par ek `PreToolUse` Claude Code hook jo 2 se exit kare jab `old_string` mein `patches.txt` ki koi existing non-comment line ho, `node --test` suite ke saath.

01-contract-validate.title: spice_lite reviewer ka Agent Contract likho aur validate karo
01-contract-validate.objective: `agents/CONTRACT_TEMPLATE.md` copy karo, `spice_lite` par `reviewer` roster agent ke liye saare gyarah fields bharo, har must aur mustNot rule ko mechanism ya convention tag karo, aur `validate-contract.mjs` ko bina warnings ke 0 se exit karwao. Pehle dekho ki validator ek realistic first attempt par kya report karta hai (invented tool, scope mein `bench console`, untagged rule, akela "hook", bina mechanism ka gate). Phir contract ko JSON `agentContracts` entry ke roop mein export karo. Module 05-agent-roster is draft ko `agents/reviewer/CONTRACT.md` ke roop mein finalise karta hai.

evaluationCriteria: Saare gyarah fields bhare hain; `validate-contract.mjs` bina warnings ke 0 se exit karta hai.
`tools` aur `permissions` agree karte hain: permissions mein kuch bhi aisa tool grant nahi karta jo `tools` chhodta hai, aur Bash scope kisi `bench` command ka naam nahi leta.
No-edit, no-delegation, git-only Bash aur no-site_config rules mechanism se enforce hain, instruction se nahi.

`dontAsk` gap maana gaya hai: `bench --site test.localhost run-tests` project allow list par hai, isliye agent-scoped Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook backstop hai (aur yeh `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `bypassPermissions` parents ke under `permissionMode` caveat ko bhi cover karta hai).
`failureConditions` empty diff, oversized diff, missing inputs, `permissions` ya whitelist change (next: security), `patches.txt` ki edited line, aur fix, test ya migrate ki request cover karti hain.
`humanGate` ek real mechanism ka naam leta hai (PR approval, `bench --site * migrate` par `ask` rule) aur batata hai ki reviewer kabhi merge approval nahi deta.
improvements: Agla template `developer` ke liye bharo; uske `tools` mein Edit, Write aur `bench --site test.localhost run-tests *` ke saath Bash hai, isliye uska `mustNot` restrict kare ki woh kahan likhta hai aur bataye ki `migrate` sirf `ask` rule ke peeche chalta hai.

Ek `--frontmatter` mode jodo jo contract se matching `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `permissionMode`) print kare, aur module 05 mein use real file ke against diff karo.
Module 05 ke likhne ke baad CI mein `agents/*/CONTRACT.md` par validator chalao.

agentContracts.purpose: `sample-app/spice_lite/` ke ek diff ko Frappe standards ke against review karo aur structured findings return karo, taaki human reviewer jaldi decide kar sake ki change mergeable hai ya nahi. Frappe app par Python change ka sirf aadha hissa hai: reviewer DocType JSON diff (fields, `permissions` array, `search_index`, `autoname`), `patches.txt`, `hooks.py` entries aur fixtures ko controllers aur whitelisted methods ke saath padhta hai. Yeh correctness, design, readability, testing aur standards cover karta hai; security aur performance concerns flag karta hai lekin unka deep analysis `security` aur `sre` agents par chhodta hai. Yeh kabhi code nahi badalta, kabhi `bench` nahi chalata, aur kabhi change approve nahi karta.
inputs: Diff karne ke liye base ref, jaise `main` (required, task message mein).
Run id, jaise `2026-09-30-feat-observation-interpretation` (required, task message mein; run folder ka naam deta hai).
Upstream handoff ka path jo change ka intent batata hai, jaise `.ai-sdlc/runs/<run-id>/04-developer.md` (optional; iske bina reviewer diff ko uske apne merits par review karta hai aur yeh bolta hai).

Apply karne wale standards: `context/standards/review-standards.md` aur `context/standards/frappe-coding-standards.md` (hamesha), `context/standards/testing-standards.md` jab `tests/` ya `test_*.py` ki files badlein, `context/standards/api-standards.md` jab `spice_lite/api/` badle.

Path-scoped rules jo Claude Code khud load karta hai jab reviewer matching files padhta hai: `*.py` ke liye `.claude/rules/spice-lite-python.md` aur DocType JSON, `patches.txt` aur `hooks.py` ke liye `.claude/rules/doctype-json.md`.
outputs: Main session ko final message: poora handoff document (YAML front matter plus handoffFormat ke sections). Orchestrator, jiske paas run folder ka Write access hai, ise `.ai-sdlc/runs/<run-id>/NN-reviewer.md` ke roop mein save karta hai.
Har finding ki ek row wali findings table: `id | severity | category | location | evidence | recommendation`, severity `critical | high | medium | low | info` mein se.

Ek "Frappe surfaces in this diff" line jo list karti hai ki diff ne DocType JSON, `patches.txt`, `hooks.py`, fixtures aur whitelisted methods mein se kise chhua, taaki insaan dekh sake ki JSON review hua, skip nahi.
Har us category ke liye explicit "no findings" line jo check ki gayi aur clean mili.
agentContracts.permissions: `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` mein frontmatter: `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash` (allowlist, isliye Edit, Write aur Agent available nahi) aur second guard ke roop mein `disallowedTools: Edit, Write, NotebookEdit`, `permissionMode: dontAsk` ke saath, jo har us cheez ko auto-deny karta hai jo prompt karti. Is repo mein iska matlab hai ki `.claude/settings.json` ke `ask` rules (`bench --site * migrate`, `console`, `execute`, `install-app`, `git commit`, `git push`) reviewer ke liye human tak pahunchne ki jagah deny ho jaate hain. Do gaps bachte hain aur module 05 mein band hote hain: `Bash(bench --site test.localhost run-tests *)` project allow list par hai, isliye `dontAsk` ab bhi reviewer ko tests chalane dega; aur jab parent session `bypassPermissions`, `acceptEdits` ya `auto` mein chalta hai tab subagent ka `permissionMode` ignore hota hai. Isliye module 05 agent ke apne frontmatter mein ek Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook jodta hai jo `git diff|git log|git status` ke bahar ke kisi bhi Bash command ke liye 2 se exit karta hai. Project deny rules (`Read(**/site_config.json)`, `Read(**/common_site_config.json)`, `Read(./.env)`, `Read(./**/*.phi.*)`, `bench drop-site`, `reinstall`) reviewer par bhi baaki har agent ki tarah apply hote hain.
must: Har finding ko saare chhe fields do: id, severity, category, `path:line` ke roop mein location, diff ya file se quote kiya evidence, recommendation. [convention: checked by the reviewer golden tasks in module 09-agent-evaluation]

Violate hua standard file plus rule number ke roop mein cite karo, jaise request path mein `frappe.get_all` ke liye `context/standards/frappe-coding-standards.md` rule 2. [convention: checked by the reviewer golden tasks]

DocType JSON, `patches.txt`, `hooks.py` aur fixture changes ko Python diff ke saath review karo, aur bina `patches.txt` entry ke schema ya data change, ya bina security step ke `permissions` array change ko kam se kam `high` rate karo. [convention: `context/standards/review-standards.md`, checked by a golden task with a seeded DocType JSON diff]
Har us category ke liye "no findings" bolo jo check ki aur clean mili. [convention: human reviewer reads the handoff]

Change ko `git diff <base>...HEAD` se padho, kisi pehle ki conversation ki yaad se nahi. [mechanism: subagents start with no conversation history; Bash is limited to git by `permissionMode: dontAsk` plus allow rules]

Aise handoff ke saath khatam karo jiske front matter mein `run_id`, `step`, `agent: reviewer`, `status`, `inputs`, `next` hon. [mechanism: the Claude Code hook `check-handoff.mjs` from module 08 rejects a handoff with missing keys]
mustNot: Koi bhi file edit, create ya delete karna, DocType JSON aur `patches.txt` samet. [mechanism: Edit and Write are absent from `tools` and listed in `disallowedTools`]
Doosre agents ko delegate karna. [mechanism: `Agent` is absent from `tools`, so the reviewer stays at depth 1]

`git diff`, `git log` ya `git status` ke alawa koi shell command chalana; khaas kar koi `bench` command nahi (run-tests, migrate, console, execute). [mechanism: `permissionMode: dontAsk` auto-denies the `ask` rules, backed by the agent-scoped Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook from module 05 that also blocks the allowed run-tests]

Apne verdict ko merge approval ki tarah pesh karna ya "LGTM", "approved" ya "ready to merge" likhna. [convention: `context/standards/review-standards.md`: the `APPROVE` verdict only means no blocking findings; merge approval is a human PR approval]

Evidence mein PHI quote karna (MRN values, names, birth dates, search terms, patient-linked observation values); sirf code aur `MRN-000123` jaise synthetic fixtures quote karo. [convention: `context/security/phi-and-secrets-policy.md`, re-checked by the security agent]

`spice_lite/api/fhir.py` `lastn()` mein marked `TEACHING-DEFECT(perf-n+1)`, ya open defects (D-1, D-3, D-6 se D-12) ko naye findings ke roop mein report karna. Unhe `sample-app/docs/KNOWN_DEFECTS.md` ke reference ke saath known bataya ja sakta hai. [convention: reviewer golden tasks include a case that checks this]
failureConditions: Base ref ke against diff khaali hai ya base ref exist nahi karta: exact `git` error ke saath `status: blocked` return karo.

Diff 40 se zyada files ya 2,000 changed lines chhoota hai: `status: needs-human` return karo aur change split karne ko kaho (reordered `field_order` wala regenerated DocType JSON bhi count hota hai; use apne commit mein maango).
Referenced standard file ya upstream handoff path exist nahi karta: missing path ka naam lete hue `status: needs-human` return karo.

Change DocType `permissions` array, `hooks.py` mein `permission_query_conditions` ya `has_permission`, `@frappe.whitelist` decorator, `ignore_permissions`, ya `spice_lite/audit.py` ko chhoota hai: review karo, lekin `next: security` set karo aur wajah batao.

Change `patches.txt` ki existing line edit karta hai: Patch Log exact line text record karta hai, isliye agle migrate par patch har country site par dobara chalega. Ise `high` finding ke roop mein report karo aur `status: needs-human` return karo.
Task reviewer se code fix karne, tests chalane, ya site migrate karne ko kehta hai: mana karo, `status: blocked` return karo aur `developer` ya `tester` ko route karne ki recommendation do.
Run `maxTurns` tak pahunch jaata hai (output partial mark hota hai): partial finding list ko complete bata kar dene ki jagah `status: blocked` return karo.
agentContracts.validation: Yeh contract `node docs/foundations/validate-contract.mjs docs/foundations/reviewer-contract-draft.md` se check hota hai (exit 0, koi warnings nahi). Reviewer output teen tarah check hota hai: handoff front matter Claude Code hook `check-handoff.mjs` se (module 08); findings `evaluations/` ke golden tasks ke against (module 09), jahan `search_patients` ko `frappe.get_list` se `frappe.get_all` par switch karne wala seeded diff frappe-coding-standards rule 2 cite karta `security` finding produce kare, aur `sl_observation.json` mein bina `patches.txt` entry ke `SL Observation.value` ka type badalne wala seeded diff rule 6 cite karta `high` `standards` finding produce kare; aur ek human spot-check ki kisi finding mein quoted evidence missing nahi hai.
agentContracts.handoffFormat: `workflows/README.md` aur style guide mein defined YAML front matter ke saath Markdown: `run_id`, `step`, `agent: reviewer`, `status` (`complete | blocked | needs-human`), `inputs` (upstream handoff file names ki list), `next` (`security`, `tester`, `developer` ya `human`). Sections is order mein: `## Summary` (ek sentence mein verdict, har severity ke counts, Frappe surfaces line), `## Findings` (six-column table), `## Decisions` (kya scope se bahar tha aur kyon), `## Open questions`, `## Artifacts` (hamesha "none written; returned to main session"). Orchestrator ise `.ai-sdlc/runs/<run-id>/NN-reviewer.md` ke roop mein save karta hai.
agentContracts.humanGate: Reviewer advisory hai; gate human pull-request approval hai. Koi bhi `critical` ya `high` finding merge block karti hai (review-standards), aur orchestrated run mein orchestrator `status: needs-human` ke saath ruk jaata hai jab tak koi insaan har ek ko accept ya reject na kare. Reviewer jo bhi produce karta hai woh kisi site ya remote tak nahi pahunchta: `git push` aur `bench --site * migrate` `.claude/settings.json` mein `ask` rules hain (reviewer ke `dontAsk` ke under seedha deny), force-push aur `bench drop-site` denied hain, aur CLAUDE.md rule 9 push, merge, shared site migrate karna aur deploy karna insaan par chhodta hai.

`docs/foundations/anatomy-breakdown-reviewer.md` mein baarah rows hain, har ek Mechanism: ya Convention: se khatam hoti hai, aur ek Frappe surfaces table hai.

Tum kabhi akela "hook" nahi likhte: yeh ya toh `hooks.py` mein Frappe hook hai ya `.claude/settings.json` mein Claude Code hook.
`node docs/foundations/grade-classification.mjs` tumhari classification ko 10/12 ya behtar score karta hai, dono hook traps samet.
`agents/CONTRACT_TEMPLATE.md` mein gyarah `## field` headings schema order mein hain aur yeh `--template` validation pass karta hai.
`docs/foundations/reviewer-contract-draft.md` `validate-contract.mjs` ko exit code 0 aur bina warnings ke pass karta hai.
Reviewer draft ka har `must` aur `mustNot` rule `[mechanism: ...]` ya `[convention: ...]` se tagged hai.
Reviewer draft `tools` se `Agent`, `Edit` aur `Write` chhodta hai, koi `bench` command grant nahi karta, aur wajah batata hai.
Reviewer draft `permissions`-array aur whitelist changes ko `security` ko route karta hai aur `patches.txt` ki edited line ko `needs-human` treat karta hai.
`humanGate` field ek real mechanism ka naam leta hai, aur shared site par `bench migrate` insaan ke paas rehta hai.
